utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before K6 comes to give evidence, there are just a few matters that I must deal with in private session, with your leave, and one or two in public session, but they really won't take very long. Private session, yes, please, if the Court approves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Now that we're in open session, Your Honour, just to inform the lawyers operating as the accused's associates that there has been a request via the accused for the return of a statement. I've been trying to contact the associates by telephone over the weekend unsuccessfully. I may have got the wrong number or the number may not have been working, but if they come to me or the case manager, who today is Ms. Wee, or to Mr. Shin, we will give them all the detail they require. On the subject of the accused's associates, can I turn, as I regularly do, to Rule 68, the provision of exculpatory material in respect of which we provided a report last week or the week before. Because of the manner in which we're dealing with Rule 68, that is on the selective and focused basis, it is very important that I keep this topic under the most careful review. I'm going to have another focused review next week. I would invite the amici to contribute any concerns they have about -- through the Court, of course, I would invite the amici to contribute any concerns they have and indeed even possibly to attend a meeting with us to make sure that nothing's being missed. And I'm quite happy, in principle, to extend the same invitation to the accused's associates if they want to meet with me, or me and some of my colleagues, to discuss Rule 68 and how we can ensure that the exercises are conducted satisfactorily. I'm more than happy to do so, and as I say, an exercise planned for next week. Your Honour, I think that's all that's pressing. We've got a few other matters, but we've also got a witness waiting to come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let us now turn to that witness. Mr. Nice, we have the summary, for which we're grateful. Given the time constraints and given that much of his evidence deals with the time with which we're normally concerned, perhaps that can be taken fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the blinds come down for his arrival.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May this witness be shown a piece of paper with a name on it, which I think has already been provided. I thought it had already been provided. There may be some misunderstanding. Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just look at this piece of paper, please. Don't read out the name on it. Just tell us if that is your correct name. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May that piece of paper be exhibited? It's not a very satisfactory piece of paper. I may get another one and substitute for it, but may it be exhibited?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 218.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness is giving evidence with protection of distortion and a pseudonym, but for matters that would reveal his identity, I would seek private session, which will, of course, always be as short as possible. But for the first paragraph on the summary of the background, may we have private session, and after that - which should only take a couple of minutes - move into open session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before we move into private session, let me make it plain to those in the public gallery and elsewhere that any publication of this witness's proper name will be a contempt and will be treated as such. Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection, because the only name mentioned by the other side was "Milosevic," and I would like to clear it up and see whether the witness is claiming this person to be a relative of mine or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is still in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Go into private session

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness K6, I think you can help us with the MUP of Kosovo in the period of the 1990s; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your experience was with state security, not with the public MUP, and you prefer to deal with the state security rather than with the public MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The state security part of the MUP in Kosovo, was it divided into a number of divisions or sectors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can introduce two exhibits. I apologise for the fact that they've had to have handwritten amendments on them, but I realised this morning that they were only in English and that it isn't helpful for the witness to have documents which don't have a language he can understand. So that the original exhibits which have been subject to the normal processing of the institution have been amended with handwritten translations, and they'll have to be re-registered in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's have the exhibits now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There should only be two. There should only be two. I've withdrawn the public one. Sorry. The first one, the public sector, we needn't trouble with. Let's deal with the state security. Sorry. My mistake for not having communicated with Ms. Wee.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit numbers 219 and 220.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we place one of them on the overhead projector, please. Can we place this one on the overhead projector. That one on the overhead projector, please. Thank you. This will be --?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 219.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: K6, does this adequately set out the overall structure of the state security Kosovo detachments in early 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see at the head of the security a box with three names in it, headed by David Gajic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the box, we see the various detachments for Pristina, Pec, Prizren, and then Kosovska Mitrovica, Gnjilane, and Urosevac. But just looking at Pristina, we see that that was itself broken down into five other detachments: Podujevo, Glogovac, Obilic, Kosovo Polje, and Lipljan, and was under the control of Lutfi Ajazi; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we go to the next exhibit, please, 220. Does this set out the subdivisions of state security in early 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The sectors by which the state security was divided we can see are 8 by number, or whether they're 8 in number, I'm not sure. Which number were you in? Which sector did you work in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: In the eighth one, number 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what the eighth sector of the state security did in the mid- to late 1990s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: In the mid-1990s, up to 1998, the main job of this sector was detection and investigation of the identity of people connected with terrorism and with the people working against the system which was headed by the accused. The person responsible for this sector was the person mentioned above, whereas I myself, I was involved in concrete activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that the sector was concerned with people working against the system. Had the sector ever had any involvement with something called political crime, or similar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Only political crimes related to terrorism, against terrorists. The investigation and detection of terrorism, terrorism as the establishment of the KLA and the appearance of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see from the chart that David Gajic was in charge. Where was he based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: He was based in Prishtina. One was responsible for coordination of security in Kosova, and without his authorisation, you couldn't do anything in -- you couldn't undertake any action anywhere in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those with more local control directly over state security operating in Pristina were who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The people are written down here, and I think the accused can see them too, the names too. If you want, I could increase the volume of the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell us, please: Was there a man called Lakovic who featured? He may not be on the document, but did he feature? And what was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Milan Lakovic, or Misku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: His pseudonym was Misku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: He was head of the Prishtina headquarters of state security and responsible for all the directives. He was particularly responsible for the functioning of the sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And Lutfi Ajazi, his role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Lutfi Ajazi was particularly responsible for detachments, under Prishtina, and was an advisor to Misku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. To what extent was Kosovo, under David Gajic, self-contained; to what extent did it have to refer elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right up to the top was under the control of David Gajic. He simply had to refer to very high sources in Serbia itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just yes or no: Did you learn to which sources in Serbia he had to refer, to which individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn to whom it was he had to refer, and over what period of time was it that you acquired this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Everyone knew about this. All information went to Stanisic for Kosova, directly to Stanisic, and the accused knows Stanisic very well, of course. I can assure you that the accused was well informed about everything, even the smallest details, on the situation in Kosova with regard to state security, through Stanisic, who was informed by David Gajic and Lakovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there units of the police known as special police units, or thought of as special police units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: State security had its own special units which were used in questions of state security, and they were such units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they based locally or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Their main base was in Belgrade, but they also had a base in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they came to Kosovo, who organised their movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Their movement was organised by a Zoran Dragovic, who was under the command of the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your working for state security, did you see any operations that were joint between them and the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Well, there was concrete action, but without their cooperation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any operations that had cooperation between the two forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: There was -- no, there was no concrete cooperation between them, because they were secret special units which did work for state security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about these secret special units that did work for state security. Did any of them have names, titles, or other ways by which they might be recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: There was a special unit called Crvene Beretke, the Red Beret group. They were based in Belgrade, in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they operate from time to time in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes. Normally, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By whom were they led when they operated in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Zoran Dragovic. I think he's mentioned later down in the text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any other known leader at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Well, they did in Belgrade, but I didn't know him. They had their commander there, yes, but we didn't have much connection with them. We were -- there was one who knew them very well, Zeka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What operations were you aware of the Red Berets carrying out, in general terms, in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Their activities were concentrated on anti-terrorism. They called it terrorism, but I can say, I can assure you, that they were committing acts of terrorism themselves. Instead of eliminating terrorism, they were creating terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We'll go into private session, and the Court will see the passage concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Mr. Milosevic, we'll get on more quickly if you don't interrupt. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go on to another topic? Did you hear from your superiors, and in particular from Misku, any expressions of attitude towards Albanians that may have affected the policy of state security or driven the policy of state security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Misku quite often said that anyone who agrees [as interpreted] with the policies of the accused would not have a place in Kosova. And the so-called terrorism and the KLA must be exterminated. This is related to what I said before, that it was very open and very much supported the policies of the accused. And he irritated the Albanians there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The way the transcript reads, K6, is that you said that "anyone --" that Misku said that "anyone who agrees with the policies of the accused would not have a place in Kosovo." I don't know if that's what you said or intended to say or if it's an error --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: No. Anyone who was not in agreement with the policies of the accused has no place in Kosova. Those who are not in agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any public statements of public figures that reflected or accorded with the views of Misku at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: There were quite a few, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any public figure in particular whose observations accorded with Misku's approach?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: There was Jaksic, Trajkovic, and quite a few others. I would say the Serb people in Kosova, they agreed with such policies. They were -- they supported the -- those policies, and that's why the situation got worse and worse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Detail, a lot of detail, a topic, Drenica. Did the state security have access to information about what was happening through Drenica and Malisheva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: State security, from the time when the KLA arose, from the very start, was informed concretely about every action and every basis they had. I'm sure of that. And I'm sure also that the accused was well-informed about all the secrets. I can assure you that the accused was informed in detail with regard to the KLA and its appearance on the scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the information that you acquired or that the service acquired on Drenica in that area from human sources or from mechanical and similar listening devices, or from both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The sources were individuals, verbally and in written reports, and also technical apparatus which was implanted in various spots with various types of apparatus. So there were various sources. And all the information was -- came together. It was joined together and compared to see how it compared with the information given by people. So the result was clear, and everything was under the control of state security as a result.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How full, how complete, did you judge the penetration of the KLA, the knowledge of the KLA had been by the mid to late 1990s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The appearance of the KLA was a necessity, because there was an apartheid system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We don't want -- if I may stop you. We don't want a political analysis. The question you were asked was: Was there a penetration of it? Could you just concentrate on that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how full was your knowledge of the KLA at that time? For example, how many people did it have? Where were they? That sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: They were concentrated primarily in Drenica, the KLA. And a small part of them but an increasing part, starting from November 1996, they began -- they had about 200 members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it have been possible at that stage and thereafter to have taken definitive action against the KLA if the state security had been so instructed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Up to that time, anything would have been possible, and they would have been eliminated. I'm sure of this. But state security in Prishtina didn't have authorisation to undertake any such activity for the elimination of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether it ever drew up plans or sought authorisation to eliminate the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Plans for the elimination of the KLA, in Drenica in particular, were made from 1991 on. But from 1996, 1997, 1998, there were concrete plans. When Drenica was attacked, there were very detailed and drafted plans, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom were these plans referred but they were never implemented?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: All such plans were referred to Serbia. What I mean is to Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I turn from those plans to the judiciary. Who were the principal judges working in your region at that time? Paragraph 19 of the summary.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The main judges -- there were three or four judges, investigators. The main one, as far as I remember, was a certain Marinkovic or Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first name of that judge? Can you remember? And gender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: I don't remember the first name, no, but I think it's written down somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a man or a woman judge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: A man. But there was also a woman. There was -- one was a woman, one was a man. There were two judges. Marinkovic was one of them. She was a woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the manner of operation of those judges, and in particular of Judge Marinkovic, so far as state security work was concerned? How did she deal with it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: I can -- I can assure you that she was involved. The employees of state security were -- would bring money to the judges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Judge Marinkovic with any person who was being dealt with as a suspect for some offence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Could we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be, of course, a unique individual, and could lead to identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In public session now, K6. You've told us a little of the involvement of one paramilitary group. Was there another group known by a particular name and associated with a particular politician that you can tell us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: There was another group active in Kosova with -- I can assure you, they had connections. This was the group of Arkan, Arkan's Tigers. Arkan was born in Kosova, as far as I know. He lived in Prishtina, in the neighbourhood of Ulpiana. His mother was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And another group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: There was also Seselj's people and the Black Hand. There were quite a few groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just describe for the judges so that they can have a picture of the involvement of these special groups. How did they dress? How did they behave in public places at this time towards Albanians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: When they came to Kosova, they behaved in such an arrogant manner. It was -- you couldn't even describe it in words. They came as so-called liberators of the Serb people. Saviors of the Serb people, they thought themselves as. Whereas the Albanians, in particular, in Drenica, Arkan and his people mistreated them terribly and behaved very arrogantly, and they were looked down upon by the population because they behaved in such a manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did they dress and how were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: They were usually dressed in black clothes, with green, and they had special emblems on their clothing, and quite openly they carried Heckler automatic rifles, mark Heckler.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: And they had vehicles, jeeps, the best vehicles you could find. They even parked their cars in people's courtyards. They didn't have any problems. Courtyards of the Albanians. No problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when they went into places like cafes and restaurants? What sort of things did they do, generally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: When they went into restaurants -- for example, in Gllogovc once, Arkan's people went into an Albanian restaurant and broke everything up. They behaved terribly. For other people, it would have been impossible to do that. And they beat people up in Gllogovc, in the restaurant there. And in Prishtina, when they went into a restaurant, they never paid their bills. They went -- even if they went into a Serb restaurant, they never paid the bill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us about -- something about the Red Berets, but tell us: As to these other groups, were they based locally and therefore a permanent presence, or did they come from time to time, and if so, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: As I said, the Red Berets weren't there. They had their bases in Serbia, and they came to Kosova from time to time if they had orders to do so, for a few days, and then returned to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know, from your work within state security, where the orders came from to bring these paramilitaries into Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Orders for the Red Beret to come into Kosova were given from Zoran Dragovic, but he worked with the other two. But he was primarily responsible for their stays in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little ambiguous. When you say "the other two," you mean the other two paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: No, no. For the other two persons I mentioned from security, the first two heads of state security. They worked with Zoran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: And Zoran was the main person responsible to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who caused either Arkan's Tigers or the Black Hand to come to Kosovo when they did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: They came either of their own will or it was the local population, local Serb population, who called them. I don't think they were ordered by -- they were under orders particularly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us about how they were dressed. Your own unit, state security, was that a civilian-clothed unit or uniformed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Civilian clothes. And there were special units, if you mean them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Their uniform, the special units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The special units had uniforms when they were in action; otherwise they were dressed in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when they were in action, what were the colour and nature of their uniforms? Can you help us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes. They were completely dressed in black. The uniforms were completely black. And their caps were red on their heads. And that's why they were called Red Berets, because of the berets on their heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What weaponry was available to the state security and for these special units when they came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The state security and the special units had the most modern arms existing at that time - short and long weapons, such as Scorpions, Hecklers, and 16-millimetre revolvers - and anti-bullet vests which were the best there were at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when it came to vehicles and armoured vehicles, were those available to security, to the MUP, at all, and if so, was it to the public as opposed to the state security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The armoured personnel carriers were owned by the public and by the public units of security. They had their own armoured carriers. Whereas the special units didn't have -- I didn't see any armoured personnel carriers with them, so I couldn't really tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, if that's a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't have a great deal more to ask of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now. Witness K6, would you remember, in this adjournment and any others there may be, not to speak to anybody about your evidence until it's over. That does include the members of the Prosecution team. We'll adjourn now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: K6, a few more short matters of detail. Just yes or no to this: Can you -- can you help at all with the fate of a man called Enver Maloku? Just yes or no. This is not in the summary. It's in the statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a sentence --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Correction: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know nothing about what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The smuggling of arms from Albania, did you get to learn anything of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Well, look, for the first time from Albania, in 1991, Adem Jashari, with five of his friends, came back to Kosova, while the weapons that were brought in Albania were mainly taken also from Serbia, were mainly purchased from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As to those coming from Albania, did state security maintain observations on what was happening? Paragraph 15 of the summary.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The weapons that came from Albania, as concerns these weapons, the state security knew everything about them. However, I repeat, they never undertook without concrete authorisation from their superiors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If steps were not taken to restrict the importation of weapons coming from Albania, why not? What reason was given for not stopping the flow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: As concerns this question, the accused would rather give a better answer. However, the main aim was that one day, an armed war should start between the KLA, meaning between the Albanian -- the army of the people -- of the Albanian people and of Serbia. This is the scenario that Serbia itself prepared and it was aware of. And its aim was totally something else. And as far as Kosova is concerned, I'm sure the accused can give a better answer to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just have a look at a couple of directories -- a couple of exhibits - I beg your pardon - to make a couple of points. First of all, a temporary telephone directory I would like you to look at, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 221.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This exhibit - thank you very much. 221 - is said to be a Republic of Serbia, Ministry of the Interior Temporary Directory of Users of Radiotelephone Links.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And it comes from the Kosovo collection of documents, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see on it that although it's Ministry of the Interior, on the first page it's got "Channels for Coordination, VJ Army." So does this help us at all with understanding the coordination between the state security and the army? Was there such coordination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: This shows the coordination between the VJ and the public security, whereas the state security was -- for example, there is only one person who would serve as coordinator with them during actions or operations, whereas the figures that I see below here are concerned with the state security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If you'd turn over four pages, please. And I know that you're concerned not to speak too much about the public security, of which you have less knowledge than the state security, but if we turn over four pages to something called code tables - do you have that? - we see a listing, under the code "yellow," of various weaponry: machine-gun Browning, impact rifle grenade, impact shaped charge shell, hand-held rocket launcher, and so on. By which group or groups were these weapons held, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Excuse me. The question is not clear to me. It's not very clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the code table that's headed "yellow"? This is the same document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see the listing of weaponry there, starting with the M-84 machine-gun and going on to the Browning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By which part of MUP forces, if either, were these weapons held, please? It includes a Praga and a recoilless gun.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The MUP forces were the public security forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these weapons were held by them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: These weapons -- yes. The police, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can we look at one other document, please -- two other documents, but first of all, this one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 222.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document from the military department at Kosovska Mitrovica, and we saw reference to that department earlier. Do you have the original in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And we can put the English on the overhead projector, the original for the witness, please, to make life easier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: At the moment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Leave the English version on the overhead projector. Sorry. I should have made it -- that's the one. And give the Serbian version to the witness to read in front of him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This, then, is a document from the military department dated the 28th of November, 1997. Pausing there: You left the state security at about what time, K6? About when?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's marked as urgent and to the Pristina military command. And at the end of the document -- I don't ask anybody to turn it over, but we can see on the English it comes from Colonel Radisa Nastic. Did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look in the first paragraph, there's only a small point I want you to help us with from this document. It says, about four lines down on the first paragraph: "In the Srbica municipality, on the 26th of November, 1997, a MUP column was ambushed and shot at with rifles, machine-guns, rocket launchers and grenades. Because of the large number of terrorists, about 50 according to our estimates, MUP helicopters were engaged." And then it goes on to deal with fierce fighting. Did MUP have access to helicopters, please, K6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the public MUP rather than your part of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: This is the public MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And then the last document, please, that I'd like you to look at, which is a document from earlier on and still within your period of service.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 223.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If the original could be placed with the witness, and we'll just put the English version on the overhead projector. We're going to be looking at different --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Original to the witness and -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the first page of this document we can see that it is dated the 19th of April. It's from the Republic of Serbia's Ministry of Interior and it goes to the Secretariat of the Interior, to all organisational units. Now, the first passage in the English version on the first page I'm not troubled with, under general Roman I. We can observe on page 3, if the usher would be so good, that one of the listed secretariats, at number 24, is Pristina. So that's your secretariat. If we go on to page 4, we come to a general heading, Roman II, in the middle of the page. Page 4, at the bottom. Thank you. And if you'd find the passage in the original that starts with the Roman II, K6, under ordinary number 1, dealing with organisation of the MUP, it says: "Proceeding from the ministry's internal organisation, internal and other communications should be carried out in the following manner: A department of internal affairs or a police station shall report all occurrences, events, and information of interest for security to the SUP to which it belongs and the secretariat to the ministry." And then over the page, please, page 5, top of the page, it allows for direct communications with the ministry or other secretariat in emergency cases. The direct communication to the Serbian Ministry of Security matters, does that accord with your experience, K6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: These things were more or less regular. Every time before the beginning of the action or operation, there was concrete information as regarded the persons who were leaders. For example, in municipalities or in detachments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You've also told us about Misku's movements. Did you learn how regularly or irregularly was he to travel to Belgrade? What was the frequency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Misku usually went to Belgrade to send their secret documents or other information. He would go on Tuesdays or Thursdays every second week. But if necessary, he would go every week. But mainly he would go on a Tuesday or a Thursday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can stay on the same page we were on, please, usher, page 5. And go down to paragraph 4. We see the following: "Police stations for the control of state border crossings send information directly to the relevant ministry -- to the relevant administration in the ministry and to the secretariat on whose territory they are located." First of all, can you help us with this: State border crossings, what's meant by that and would any boundary between Kosova and Serbia be included in that definition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: No. This does not include the boundaries between Kosova and Serbia. This includes every border checkpoint. The -- he was responsible, and he would hand in information to every border checkpoint in every municipality he would go to, and then the relevant bodies would send it further to their supervisor bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you were in this service, were there checkpoints between Kosova and Serbia or not? And if you can't remember, say so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: At the time when I worked, between Kosova and Serbia there was no border checkpoint. There was one. However, there was none that served as a mere border checkpoint and that was under control all the time. As far as such a thing is concerned, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then finally, over the page to page 6 and to paragraph 7. Reference to Serbia and Montenegro now. "Communication between secretariats in the Republic of Serbia and corresponding organisational units in the Republic of Montenegro will be carried out through the ministry..." that is through the ministry in Belgrade. Did you have any experience of that happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Normally, yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discover - this is page 9 of the statement, not of the summary - did you discover one way or another whether the orders that you were receiving, you say from Stanisic, effectively, incorporated decision-making with Montenegro or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: No. The decision-making regarding Kosova, even though he was responsible for Montenegro as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My mistake. I don't understand quite your answer. It may be my question. Was there any involvement of Montenegro in the decisions that were made about the MUP in Kosova?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Such a thing I learned from my colleagues, that is the fact that even the Albanian employees of the state security who quit working or were dismissed were also -- part of them were also those who worked in Montenegro as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think I'm going to get much further on that, and I'm not going to take time on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: K6, you are in a position, I think, to give an account, if it's relevant and if anybody wants to hear about it, of the origins and development of the KLA - just yes or no - as you understood it to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes, except I would like for it to be a private session, if it's possible. If not, it's still okay, but anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask about it. I'm just checking to see if you're in a position to deal with that if necessary. The second thing is you left --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- you left the service in 1998, I think, or 1997, 1998, and you can give an account of what happened to you and your family if asked and if it's relevant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: I can. Except that that has to be a closed session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on page 4 of the summary, paragraph 2 of the Roman II sub-heading "Proofing sessions." Just a couple of questions about one particular event and joint -- and joint operations. Just yes or no: Did you learn about what happened at the Jashari family compound? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that stage, had you already left the service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: At the time, I had not left the service, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you learn about this event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Could this go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll come back to it in -- perhaps we can go into private session for that straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I want it. Yes, I do. But I should like to have more time than the opposite side, because the witness has a statement of 25 pages. That's how long it is. And I don't think it's fair for you to give me the same amount of time as the Prosecution had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The same amount. If at the end you've made good use of your time, you can make an application for more, but I'm not going to encourage it, given the nature of his evidence. An hour and a half, which you will have, should be more than sufficient. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. How much time do I have, then? Could you tell me? Because sometimes -- how much? How long?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's very little time for such an extensive statement, Mr. May, but I shall do my best and endeavour to do so. I hope the witness will give short answers, but I do hope that you will extend that time for me, because an hour and a half is not enough. But let's move on to the questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to your knowledge, the KLA planned an assassination attempt on Rugova; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It's correct. And further on -- may I extend my answer as concerns this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Not for the moment. Let's try and keep the answers short, please, and we can get through the evidence more quickly. There will be a chance at the end for the Prosecution to take up any points which they think relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He said so. He said it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The KLA rejected people who supported Rugova; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: This is partly correct. When I say "partly," then I might as well answer yes, due to time reasons. Partly, I repeat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. According to your information and knowledge, in the operations of the KLA, Turks, Iranians, Bosnians, and so on, they all took part; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It's correct that there were Iranians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Turks and Bosnians as well; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Otherwise, according to your knowledge and information, Jakup Krasniqi said that there were a lot of Islamic elements from Iran, Turkey, and other elements in the KLA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: I do not believe this was the case as regards what you are saying; however, the main aim was to have Kosova freed once and for always. That's as much as we know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to remind you to answer my questions. And on page 24, in the one-but-last paragraph of your statement, it says, and I am going to read it: "Among the Albanians, there is panic being disseminated since Jakup Krasniqi said, a long while ago, that there were Islamic elements in the KLA, such as people from Iran, Turkey, and other countries." Therefore, that is something that you yourself stated. Do you stand by that or are you changing your testimony now? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: I have nothing to change.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Krasniqi and Sulejman Selimi, for example, said that unless -- if NATO does not supply us with weapons, we will continue and obtain funds and supplies from our Islamic brothers. That's what you say. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It's correct that he stated such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is it correct that they didn't select their methods in liquidating people, they didn't choose their methods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Of course, like only Serbs can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And otherwise, a successful operation, according to KLA criteria, for which money was received, was if policemen were killed. That was considered successful. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: According to them, every killing of policemen was a success. However, I may say that the KLA also defended the population. This was the reason why the KLA came up on the political scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give me an answer to what I'm asking you? Is that correct, what I asked you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: [In Serbian] Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because it says here, on page 22, paragraph 3, they were given 5.000 German marks for every successful operation, and "successful" meant, i.e., where police were killed. All right. Let's move on. Operations in 1998, and especially towards the end of 1998, were organised by Hashim Thaci, Sulejman Selimi, Rexhep Selimi, Jakup Krasniqi and Sokol Bashota; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The attacks were coordinated and organised every time. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of these individuals, right, the ones that I just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Only -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Where there were no police attacks, they organised their own attacks on peaceful villages; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. On page 23, the second sentence in the last paragraph states the following: "In places where there were no police attacks, they organised their own attacks on peaceful villages." I've read out the whole sentence, from the capital letter to the full stop at the end of it. So is it true or not? That's your statement. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: [In Serbian] No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you are retracting this portion of your statement, you're going back on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have to find it. Just a moment. We'll have to find it in the English first of all. Mr. Nice, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I haven't caught up with the accused on this at the moment. He says it's on page 23.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbian version it is on page 23, and it is the last paragraph, second sentence, which states: "In --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Page 24 of the English, I think, and I think it's in the second paragraph. Yes. There we are.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The paragraph starts with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're going to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The witness may be able to follow it in the B/C/S version I've got. I think he may be able to deal with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Put it in front of him, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Perhaps I can hand that to him. One coming. And if he can follow it in the B/C/S, then if the accused will give him a chance to find the references in the B/C/S version, we'll probably be able to find them in English, bearing in mind that English is generally a little longer in text than B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please bear in mind that when I am quoting the statement, I quote it word for word, and we have never established that I have ever quoted anything incorrectly. So checking this out only wastes time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But it's not suggested that you've misquoted it. If it was, it would be said. But what must happen, as a matter of fairness to a witness, is that if a passage is put to him, he should have the opportunity of seeing it so that he can deal with it. Now, then, Witness K6, have you found the passage which has been referred to: "In places where there were no police attacks, they organised their own attacks on peaceful villages." Now, would you like to give us your comment on that? That's what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it possible to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, if it's -- let the witness go into private session, if it's necessary. Yes, briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you brief questions. Give me brief yes or no answers, please, before we go into checking them, and then we'll see. They would take some men from some houses and they would beat them unconscious. Is that right? Is that what you say? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Those who were members of the service or cooperated with the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the KLA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes. They did what I said they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They burnt houses, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: [In Serbian] No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say they didn't?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: [In Serbian] After the war. After the war, not now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said they didn't. They attacked the Berisha family in the village of Dobra Voda; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It is for a fact, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The KLA shot otherwise at Leke Berisha's house, who was -- he was a teacher; is that right? Albanian teacher.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And the same fate was one that was experienced by the Buzhalla family. They - their house was completely burnt and the whole family taken out; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the KLA and Bardhec Laci, who taught gymnastics in Klina, they did the same to his house. His house was burnt down too; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes. Normally, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They wanted to kill Leke Berisha and Bardhec Laci. So that's true, is it? And since you have relativised the answer to a series of questions, my series of questions, I'm going to read just this last paragraph for us to be able to grasp the entirety. So this is all contained in one paragraph: "Until the end of 1998, all these operations were conducted at the direction and organised by people like Jakup Krasniqi, Sulejman Selimi, Rexhep Selimi, Hashim Thaci, and Sokol Bashota. In places where there were no police attacks, they organised their own attacks on peaceful villages. They would take some men from some houses and they would beat them unconscious. Sometimes they would burn houses, particularly houses of rich people. For example, in the village of Dobra Voda where they attacked the Berisha family, they beat them and tried to kill them in the belief that they had all their wealth from the Serbs. These members of the KLA wanted to murder Leke Berisha who was an Albanian-language teacher. They burnt his house. Other villages that suffered the same fate were Cerovik where there was the Buzhalla family. They brought out all the family and burnt their house and told them they would do the same to them as they do for the Shka, an insulting expression for Serbs. The same happened to Bardhec Laci from Dobra Voda, who was a physical education teacher in Klina. They beat him up and intended to kill him because he did not allow members of the KLA to run a battle line through his house. They burnt his house. Laci and his family were saved only because of the intervention of other villagers." Therefore, these are all the questions that I asked and linked up, and you gave a positive response and replied in the affirmative. Now, let's move on. Luz Buzhalla, his house was also burnt; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true they not only burnt his house but that Hashim Thaci drew lines on his chest with knives? He drew different drawings on his chest, using knives. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Witness K6, why, if it's not correct, is it in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I please remind -- may I remind the witness and ask him questions? I have the right to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Amongst the individuals who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I've asked him a question. I've asked him a question. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go into closed session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Let's -- go on, Mr. Milosevic. We'll get an explanation due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Among the other people who the KLA beat up were -- other persons beaten by the KLA include Luz Buzhalla from Cerovik who worked as a traffic policeman in Pristina. They burnt his house. They also drew lines on his chest with knives. Hashim Thaci did this. They said to him: `You used to work in the police, and that's what you did to people.'" I'm going to skip over the next portion where it says: "Fortunately from Luz [as interpreted] the journalist Pren Buzhalla from Zadar arrived and Pren was a friend of Rexhep Selimi and saved him from death." I read it in so that you don't accuse me of getting it wrong. And then you go on to say: "There were many such cases, particularly against wealthy people, involving their shops and homes. Their property was burnt and destroyed. This was done by the KLA persons I have mentioned. Sokol Bashota is from Cerovik. The Selimi brothers have a house near the train station at Klina," and so on and so forth. That is how your statement reads. Is that correct? And that there were much such cases as I quoted from your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Could we please go into closed session?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, because this has nothing to do with the witness's identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can see at the beginning of the next paragraph what may be troubling the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness K6, as you'll appreciate, it is difficult in the extreme to conduct an examination going in and out of private session. We have considered what is appropriate. Now, the only occasion on which a private session is appropriate is if there is any risk of your identity being revealed. We cannot, for the moment, see what is involved in this, but we will allow this as a last occasion to see if there is any risk of your identity being revealed by the answer. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the KLA caused some incidents to provoke the police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: [In Serbian] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that the KLA burnt whole villages in order to conceal some of its own crimes? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: [In Serbian] No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, there were many cases where the KLA killed some family members, and the families were not allowed to talk about this for fear that they would be killed. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you challenged my previous question, let me just read out the beginning of the one but last paragraph on page 24. It is one paragraph after the one that we read out a moment ago and it states the following: "The KLA would cause some of these incidents to provoke the police to attack and burn villages and thereby cover up some of their own crimes. There would be many cases where persons have had members of their family killed by the KLA, but they would not dare speak out for fear of being murdered."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, Mr. Robinson, and Mr. Kwon. I am drawing your attention to this fact, to this portion which says that witnesses were not allowed to speak out because they were afraid they would be killed by the KLA, and I would suggest that in light of this fact, that you assess the value of this witness which the opposite side is bringing forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us go on rather than making speeches. We can read it for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it true that other incidents have -- which they conducted have been attributed to the police? For example, bombs in the Pristina cafe. Is that true? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Persons like Hashim Thaci did none of these things because of the interest of people, of their own people, but rather for their own personal interests or the interests of certain individuals. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: They operated upon their own interests and the interests of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to Hashim Thaci? That's who I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: [In Serbian] Yes. [In Albanian] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like to remind you of your sentence in the middle of this paragraph. And let me read the entire sentence: "The Serbs are capable of doing anything in the interests of their own people, while Hashim Thaci does these things out of personal interest or the interests of certain individuals who he appointed to his own government without asking the people or anyone else." Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that these people from the KLA are responsible for the murder of Ahmet Krasniqi who was the Minister of Defence in Bukoshi's government in exile? Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that Ahmet Krasniqi was killed by Milaim Zeka? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: That I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says in your statement: "This was done by Milaim Zeka on the instructions of Rexhep and Sulejman Selimi." So this was done pursuant to the orders of Rexhep and Sulejman Selimi, and we know who they are. So pursuant to their orders, Milaim Zeka killed Ahmet Krasniqi. This is what it says in your statement at the bottom of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just read the next sentence. "This has been published," it says, "in the Kosovo paper in Zurich." Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This group also has a list of people that should be murdered. Mr. May, he doesn't say that he's referring to the Bota Sot newspaper. He's saying -- he's describing what had happened and adds that this was also published in the Albanian paper that is published in Zurich.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can read it, and we have his response. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, the KLA undertook actions that had nothing to do with the alleged Serb offences on Albanian villages in Kosovo. However, occasionally this was done by the KLA simultaneously. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The KLA would receive attacks where they expected the police to attack them and not offensive against the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, can this pertain to what you wrote in the last paragraph on page 24? This is the following paragraph after the one that I quoted, and it says so in the first sentence: "These actions of the KLA were undertaken unrelated to the offensives of Serbian forces on the Albanian villages in Kosovo. However, this was happening during the same time." Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your information, Rexhep Qosja, Hyadjet Hyseni, Luljeta Pula, and Adem Demaci were more interested in their own position than in the interests of the people of Kosovo. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And based on your own information, there were even people who had to send in one car a month to the KLA and turn it over either to Hashim Thaci or Krasniqi or Bashota; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you don't know, let me remind you. Here, on page 24, just two paragraphs above, it says: "This man," and this is somebody living in Macedonia, "who came in with his wife, had to send the KLA a car every month and hand it over either to Bashota, Thaci, or Krasniqi. He sent more than 12 cars to the KLA. The wife of this man is the sister of Leke Berisha, who is currently in Macedonia," and so on and so on. Don't let me waste time any more. Did I refresh your memory sufficiently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brothers Kryeziu, Albanians, together with their sons, near Kijevo, were killed by Hashim Thaci, Rexhep Selimi, and Jakup Krasniqi; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please: Do you know how did Hashim Thaci obtained his nickname "Snake," "Zmija"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: The name of "Snake," I believe he took that name on because of Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand your answer, but let us not waste any more time. So these brothers Kryeziu, who, as you say, were killed by the people whose names I just read out, they had a gas station and they had a lot of money; is that right? Was that the main motive for their murder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Correct. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1997, there was an attack on a police station in Glogovac, in Podujevo, that was also organised by the KLA; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in that attack on Glogovac, in addition to Selimi brothers, Hashim Thaci participated as well; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And based on your information, brothers Jashari, Hamze and Adem, in 1994, once again commenced terrorist activities directed against various targets: police, civilians, and so on. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Against the police and the police cooperators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you call police collaborators those Albanians who worked in state service; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: No. Collaborators are others. It is those persons who would give information regarding the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So Jashari, Hamze and Adem, in 1995, started planning attacks on police stations and policemen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that year, when a police station in Podujevo was attacked, that was done by the Jasharis, Sulejman Selimi, and Azir Pajaziti; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Azir Pajaziti. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, there was an attack on the police station in Glogovac, when two policemen were killed and four seriously wounded, and that was also done by Adem Jashari and Rexhep Selimi; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: By the KLA. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm saying Adem Jashari and Rexhep Selimi. Is that right? Yes, KLA that is certainly, but I'm specifying the names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Correct. He was also the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And in 1966 [sic], Adem Jashari and the current commander of the KLA, Zeka, attacked the police checkpoint near Gornja Klina and killed two policemen; is that right? I apologise. I said "1966." It was in 1996. I meant to say 1996, and it was a slip of the tongue. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: They were from the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know they were from the KLA, but what I'm asking you: Is that true that in 1996 they killed two policemen when they attacked the checkpoint near Klina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Normally, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ejup Bajgora, Albanian, was killed by Rexhep Selimi and Adem Jashari; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: He was killed, but I do not know exactly from whom. It is correct that he was killed, but I don't know who did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says, in paragraph 4, page 22: "Rexhep and Sulejman Selimi and Adem Jashari were given a task to conduct an operation in western Kosovo, in Pec and Kline. In June of 1997, Selimi and Adem Jashari, as well as Pata [phoen]," which is a nickname of one of them, "killed an inspector of state security, Ejup Bajgora, in front of his own house." This is what it says in your statement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in 1997, eight policemen were killed and that it is well known that Rexhep Selimi participated in these murders, together with Adem Jashari and Azir Pajaziti? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right. Yes, people of the KLA took part. It was not the civilian population who participated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not bringing into question whether it was the KLA. I'm specifying the name. So it was Adem Jashari, Hamze Jashari, and the brother of Adem Jashari; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So based on your information, Hamze Jashari, when the conflict broke out in Prekaz, the much-mentioned conflict, was together with Adem Jashari in the house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, based on your information, that Hamze Jashari intended to surrender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: According to what I heard from my connections, it has been right like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, Adem Jashari threatened to kill him if he were to surrender; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: This is what the police has been declaring through the connections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the first one to shoot on the police was Adem Jashari; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he threaten the entire family? Did he say that he was going to kill them if they surrendered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: According to the walkie-talkies and the information given by the police, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just in order to remind you about the conversation between Adem -- and this can be found in your statement on page 23. "The conversation between Adem and his family, I heard about this from an informant and a boy, a 10-year-old son of Adem, who survived the incident and told about this to the members of the KLA. He was told never to repeat this to anybody else because his father was a hero for his own people," and so on and so on. You go on to say that the fighting continued for another two days, after which the police withdrew, which is of no relevance for this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: After the assassination of Adem Jashari and his family, the police retreated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I read you this fragment. That's true? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the fact that the boy was told never to repeat this to anyone else; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: It's not right. He has been told that his father was a hero.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but the boy was also told never to tell anyone about what had happened and that his father wanted to kill the entire family. Is that right or not? The boy was told not to tell anyone about this because his father was allegedly a hero.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: And he's really a hero.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean because he killed that many Albanians and Serbs, as you just confirmed to us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're not going into an argument about this. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1998, Rexhep Selimi and Zeka carried out an operation against the police station in Klina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during 1996 and 1997, the KLA conducted many operations against the police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also true that the KLA killed Skender Gashi, an Albanian from Glogovac, in 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: He has been an employee of the police, and it is true that they have killed him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the KLA killed Gashi in 1997; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Sokol Bashota took part in that murder as well, and his secret code-name was "Number Eleven"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: I don't know it for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's what you wrote down in your statement: "Sokol Bashota participated in that murder. Bashota's secret code-name was 'Number Eleven.'" This can be found on page 21, last paragraph: "Sokol Bashota was involved in this murder. Bashota's code-name was 'Number Eleven.' The KLA used numbers to identify some of their people." And then you go on to say: "There were other murders as well in 1996, which were mentioned in the newspapers. Members of the KLA killed about 20 people in 1997, when the conflict began to escalate." Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: KLA has killed those people who have been employees of the police and those people who have cooperated with the police. It has been a revenge. [In Serbian] Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking about what you said here, that they killed 20 people in 1997. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K6
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
